Use toilet paper rolls around your seedlings as a fort from pill bugs. If you want to stay organic or even just cheap, get some neem oil. Bugs

Pillbugs are usually beneficial. They break down organic material. They generally only damage very young plants. My suggestion would be to protect young plants for the first few weeks with the toilet paper roll as someone suggested, as well as adding some organic material like good compost or leaves for them to eat. They will turn this into nutrients usable for your plants.

If you have an abundance of pill bugs, you probably have slugs as well. Normally I only see pill bugs go after plants that have been damaged by slugs. I normally trap slugs in small bowls of beer, and use finely ground egg shells in rings around small plants.

Diatomaceous earth works for insects that have hard exoskeletons and will crawl through it. It really has to be applied with a duster to be effective, sprinkling it doesn't have the same effect of creating a microscopic field of razor blades. Without a duster, a wire mesh kitchen strainer can work. Sift it up wind of the plants and let it drift so that the will statically attach to the plant leaves.

Neem oil works for most insects. Mix it per the instructions and spray it on in the evenings, avoiding the flowers or you won't get good pollination. It works really well against pests that attack greens.

Pyrethrin works the same way as Neem oil, but is a contact insecticide. Use it in the evenings. If you use it during the day, it will kill any bees or beneficial wasps that land on the plants.

As for beneficial wasps, plant some flowers that attract them. Queen Anne's lace, dill, fennel, pretty much anything from the apiaceae family. These guys are going to be the best long term deterrent to things like aphids.
